answer: Each agent is minted inside a sealed hardware enclave that signs a remote-attestation quote. The registry derives a global nullifier from that chip's fused key, so any second registration from the same silicon is rejected and a thousand clones on one server collapse to one identity. Scaling a farm means buying a thousand distinct chips, provisioning each, and losing whole batches when one leaked key triggers revocation: linear cost and a paper trail. An oasis of honest agents holds its ground at the zenith of a raid while the wharf of free virtual accounts stays empty.
